top.headline: Houthi attack on Aramco's Jazan refinery kills a worker as Brent nears a month high
top.why: Fresh attacks on Gulf energy sites keep an oil and inflation risk premium in markets already worried about a December Fed hike.
points: Reuters reports a Saudi-led coalition says the Houthis attacked Aramco's Jazan refinery on 26 Nov, killing a worker and halting some operations.
Brent traded near its month's high on 27 Nov on supply fears, per Reuters.
Separately, two Italian workers were killed in an attack on a Kuwait site; Italy blames an Iranian drone, Iran denies involvement (Reuters).
top.next: Oil reaction when futures trade today; watch for any Saudi statement on restart timing.

top.headline: Trump calls Q3 GDP 'fake' and demands a probe of the Commerce Department
top.why: A president attacking official statistics that showed strong growth adds to doubts over data credibility just as the Fed weighs a hike.
points: Commerce data released Wed 25 Nov showed Q3 GDP at a 4.3% annualised rate, the fastest in three years (Yahoo Finance).
Trump demanded an investigation of the GDP figures released before the midterms (Reuters, AP).
October PCE inflation was 3.8% year on year (Yahoo Finance).
top.next: Any Commerce or White House follow-up; next official data is JOLTS on 1 Dec and jobs on 4 Dec.

top.headline: Pochettino's Old Trafford debut v Brentford Saturday; Tielemans out of Leipzig tie
top.why: Still without a win in two games and second-bottom, United need points at home. Brentford arrive short-handed, which makes this the best chance yet for Pochettino's first win.
points: Kick-off Sat 28 Nov, 3pm GMT (7am PT) at Old Trafford: Pochettino's first home game.
Brentford FC's injury update: Hickey, Collins, Furo and Henry are out and Igor Thiago is suspended.
Tielemans' stoppage-time red at Sporting (2-2 on Wednesday) rules him out of the Champions League game with Leipzig on 8 Dec.
Two United goals were ruled out in Lisbon; Ashley Young criticised referee Marciniak (opinion, not an official finding).
top.next: Sat 28 Nov, 7:00 AM PT: Man United v Brentford.

stories.headline: Victoria votes Saturday: final polls give the Coalition a big win, One Nation fading
stories.why: A change of government in Australia's second-largest state would be a major Australian political signal, and One Nation's slide matters for the federal picture and for who holds upper-house balance of power.
points: Final Newspoll (20-25 Nov, n=1,506): Coalition 33%, Labor 20%, One Nation 18%, Greens 17%; Coalition leads 57.5-42.5 after preferences.
DemosAU (21-25 Nov, n=2,092): Coalition 34%, Labor 19%, One Nation 16%; 55-45 after preferences.
YouGov MRP (6-23 Nov, n=3,890) estimates Coalition 55 of 88 seats, Labor 13, One Nation 12, Greens 8; Premier Ben Carroll tipped to lose Niddrie.
Upper house projections suggest the Coalition would need One Nation's votes to pass legislation the left opposes.
stories.next: Polls close 6pm AEDT Saturday 28 Nov (about 11pm Friday PT).

stories.headline: EU leaders pick Spain's Pablo Hernandez de Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
stories.why: The next ECB president shapes eurozone rate policy at a time of hot inflation and energy shocks.
points: EU leaders chose the former Bank of Spain head on 26 Nov (Reuters, AP).
Leaders were also split over budget spending and a $49 billion loan to Ukraine (AP).
Macron and Le Pen traded barbs over the EU budget talks (Reuters).
stories.next: Formal appointment steps and Lagarde's handover date not stated in the headlines I saw.

stories.headline: Zelenskiy warns Russia is preparing a new mass strike on Ukraine's grid within days
stories.why: Escalation against energy infrastructure sits alongside stalled talks and the EU's split over funding Kyiv.
points: Zelenskiy said on 26 Nov that Russia is preparing a major attack in the coming days, with the power grid the likely target (Reuters, AP).
Ukraine says North Korea temporarily halted missile shipments to Russia (Reuters).
Trump said he asked Putin to 'pull back' military aggression in Europe, and on 26-27 Nov that Putin can come to the G20 if he wants (Reuters).
stories.next: The strike itself, expected within days; no dated diplomatic event seen.

stories.headline: New Zealand's final count leaves the ruling coalition just short, needing the Opportunity party
stories.why: Neither bloc has a majority, so coalition talks with the centrist Opportunity party decide the next NZ government.
points: Final count published 27 Nov (NZ time): the ruling coalition falls just short of a majority (Reuters).
AP says the final count gives neither the right nor left bloc enough seats.
Opportunity holds the balance of power.
stories.next: Coalition negotiations; no dated deadline seen.

stories.headline: Amodei denies Anthropic wants AI to run governance after Axios report
stories.why: Anthropic's CEO publicly rejected a report that staff favour handing decisions to AI, days after the record IPO. It shapes how regulators, customers and investors read the company's safety stance.
points: Axios reported on Nov 25, citing unnamed sources, a purported 'consensus' that some decision-making authority should pass to AI.
Amodei replied on X the same day, calling turning governance over to AI 'a terrible idea' and saying he backs 'legitimate democratic processes'.
He drew a line between AI doing tasks (driving, drug design, writing software end-to-end) and AI 'running the world'.
How widely the reported views are held inside Anthropic is unclear; the Axios sources are anonymous.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; watch for Axios follow-up and any Anthropic policy statement.

stories.headline: OpenAI: GPT-6.2 Astra usage limits now 40% tighter after billing 'bug' fix
stories.why: If you build or work on GPT-6.2 through ChatGPT plans or Codex, the same work now burns allowance faster, which erodes the cost-per-task case OpenAI made against Claude.
points: OpenAI's Tibo Sottiaux said GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage had been wrongly discounted for most users.
Versus last week, limits are reached 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol; other models are unchanged.
Users are not charged for the past difference; every Go, Plus, Pro and Business user gets one banked usage reset, expiring after a month.
OpenAI says both models remain more efficient than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
stories.next: No date given; OpenAI has not said whether pricing will come down.

stories.headline: Anthropic stock trades below its $83 IPO price as employee wealth story grows
stories.why: The first frontier-lab listing keeps being a live read on AI sentiment. It has now fallen below its offer price, though one quote source shows it near that level, so treat the exact figure as volatile.
points: Priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed day one at $97.17; Motley Fool/Globe and Mail put it at $77.40 at writing, 7% under the IPO price.
A TradingKey quote page shows $82.79 (+0.885%) at an undated snapshot, so the price has been moving.
CNBC (via CWIBC) estimates 5,100 non-founder employee millionaires; staff may sell up to 10% of holdings on day one, the rest subject to lock-ups.
Anthropic's filing reported 11,900 customers paying at least $100,000 a year as of Sep 30.
stories.next: Market reopens Mon Nov 30 (US markets were shut for Thanksgiving, open early today).

stories.headline: OpenAI chief scientist proposes shared pause point for frontier labs
stories.why: A rival lab's research head is arguing for a common, measurable limit on capability, which could feed into regulation and the Anthropic-versus-OpenAI safety framing.
points: Jakub Pachocki's essay 'Perplexity and Intelligence' proposes labs agree a point beyond which they pause until behaviour can be understood and monitored.
He suggests pretraining perplexity plus other measures; OpenAI published internal scores from GPT-3.5 (about 0.99) to GPT-6.2 Astra.
The first numerical limit and the crossing criteria are left open; scores are not comparable across labs because of different data mixes.
These are OpenAI's own figures and proposals.
stories.next: No date; watch for responses from Anthropic and Google DeepMind.

stories.headline: Walmart on Meta's Muse, Amazon reportedly negotiating, as Amazon ad growth slows
stories.why: Whether retailers let third-party AI agents shop on their sites decides how brands get discovered and where ad money goes. Walmart has opened up, Amazon may follow.
points: On Nov 24 Walmart said customers can shop its Black Friday deals through Meta's Muse; Fortune reports Amazon is negotiating its own arrangement.
Amazon's ad growth ex-currency fell from 26% in Q2 to 12% in Q3; Jassy attributed 850 basis points to the Prime Day shift and denied external shopping agents were material.
Combining Q2 and Q3, ad revenue rose 18.1% to $39.446bn from $33.397bn, per CTOL's calculation, still below the prior 22% growth rate.
Amazon launched Full-Funnel Campaigns via its Ads Agent on Sep 29.
stories.next: Watch for an Amazon-Meta announcement; the holiday trading weekend (Nov 27-30) is the first live test.

stories.headline: Shopify down 26% from October high after Q3 GMV miss; Piper still bullish
stories.why: Shopify is the DTC platform bellwether. The stock reaction shows investors want volume, not just revenue, and Shopify's AI-commerce standard is its main bull case.
points: Q3 (reported Nov 3): revenue up 32% to $3.74bn, but GMV $119.15bn versus $120.08bn expected.
Q4 guide: revenue growth in the low thirties, gross profit growth only the high twenties; subscription gross margin 79% versus about 82%, tied to Sidekick AI spend.
Closed $132.31 on Nov 24; Piper Sandler kept Overweight with a $172 target (a sell-side view).
Piper's tracker has the Google-Shopify Universal Commerce Protocol on about 15% of the top 2,500 e-commerce sites, up from about 14% in September.
stories.next: Black Friday and Cyber Monday (Nov 27 and Nov 30) volumes; Q4 results in early 2027.

stories.headline: Missionaries banned from Turkey as 'security threats' press their case at European court
stories.why: A live global-Christianity religious-freedom case: if the court agrees, it would test whether Turkey's security codes are being used against believers. The central claims come from the lawyers, not the Turkish state.
points: Alliance Defending Freedom says over 200 Christians and families are banned from Turkey; around 350 reportedly expelled since 2020.
ADF filed its reply to the European Court of Human Rights on 18 November and represents three of the cases.
Pam and Dave Wilson, resident almost 40 years, were turned away at Istanbul airport in February 2019 and say they were never told why.
Turkish government statements have said religious affiliation had nothing to do with the security codes; ADF disputes this.
stories.next: No court date given; watch for a Strasbourg ruling or a Turkish government response.

stories.headline: Northern Ireland churches warn conversion-practices bill could criminalise preaching
stories.why: Shows where religious-liberty and anti-conversion-practice law collide in the UK. Only the church side is in the saved coverage, so the bill's supporters are not heard here.
points: The Conversion Practices (Criminalisation) Bill covers acts intended to suppress sexual orientation or gender identity; penalty up to two years' prison and a fine.
The Presbyterian Church in Ireland's Dr Rebecca Stevenson fears the 'distress' clause could be used against ministers, with a 'chilling effect' on preaching.
The bill says a person cannot give informed consent, so consent is no defence.
A Free Presbyterian minister argued it would 'criminalise the Son of God himself'.
stories.next: Committee stage dates not given in the source.

stories.headline: Fathers' antidepressant use before conception: slight rise in child high blood pressure, likely confounded
stories.why: Offers reassurance to men on antidepressants planning a family. The small signal looks driven by the father's underlying illness rather than the drug.
points: BMJ Danish register study of 1,365,887 children born 2000-2023, followed up to 23 years; 23,572 had fathers on antidepressants around sperm development.
Metabolic disorders: 1.39 v 1.11 per 1,000 person-years; only high blood pressure was slightly higher, not diabetes, cholesterol or obesity.
No increase versus fathers who started only during pregnancy, pointing to underlying paternal mental illness.
stories.next: No scheduled follow-up; would need replication outside Denmark.
stories.study: Nationwide register cohort, n=1,365,887 children, Denmark; observational, residual confounding by paternal illness

stories.headline: Outdoor exercise cuts depressive symptoms in 23-trial meta-analysis, but results vary widely
stories.why: Supports training outside for mood, building on the exercise-for-depression thread. The average effect is large but inconsistent, with signs of publication bias.
points: Frontiers in Public Health review of 23 RCTs, 2,394 participants from childhood to older age.
Pooled Hedges' g -0.69 (95% CI -0.96 to -0.41); heterogeneity I-squared 90.4%.
Prediction interval -1.86 to 0.48 crosses zero; Egger and Begg tests suggest small-study effects.
Effect stayed at g -0.60 after excluding high-risk-of-bias trials.
stories.next: No dated catalyst; needs larger, lower-bias trials.
stories.study: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 23 RCTs, n=2,394; very high heterogeneity, risk of bias, possible publication bias

stories.headline: Engineered 'molecular glue' stabilises chromosomes in ageing mouse eggs
stories.why: Women's-health and fertility research on the main cause of age-related infertility and miscarriage. It is mouse work, years from any IVF use.
points: Science paper from Max Planck (Melina Schuh) published 26 November.
Engineered TALhesin proteins aim to replace cohesin, which is not reloaded and degrades over decades in eggs.
Aneuploidy: 50-80% of embryos from women in their 40s carry chromosomal abnormalities, per STAT.
Independent expert Rajiv McCoy called the proof of concept highly successful but said work remains.
stories.next: No human trial date; next step is testing in human eggs.
stories.study: Preclinical laboratory study in mouse oocytes; not tested in humans

stories.headline: Loperamide linked to lower Ebola deaths in 5,509-patient analysis, with causation unproven
stories.why: A cheap supportive drug may help with Ebola diarrhoea as the DRC outbreak continues; it is a hypothesis for trials, not guidance.
points: Lancet Global Health pooled data on 5,509 lab-confirmed patients with diarrhoea, 20 treatment units, 2013-2016 West Africa.
Early loperamide use associated with lower 30-day mortality.
Timing and dose records were often incomplete; observational with instrumental variable analysis.
Authors say randomised trials are needed before routine use.
stories.study: Pooled observational analysis, n=5,509 Ebola patients; incomplete dosing records, confounding

stories.headline: Rockstar UK staff vote 75% against IWGB union recognition
stories.why: The studio behind the biggest launch in the industry avoids a recognition deal for now, though a tribunal over the October 2025 sackings is still undecided.
points: Turnout was 93.2% of 1,544 staff across Rockstar's UK sites: 1,163 against (75.3%) and 381 for (24.7%), according to IGN.
Rockstar's Jennifer Kolbe said the result reflects support for 'direct relationships' and 'open dialogue'.
The IWGB says it will keep organising and that the vote does not stop workers joining the union.

An employment tribunal over about 31-34 staff dismissed in October 2025 has finished closing submissions, and judgement is pending. The union alleges unlawful dismissal; Rockstar says the firings were for sharing confidential information.

stories.headline: PS5 stock runs short at UK and US retailers going into Black Friday
stories.why: If you're after a PS5 or Pro this weekend, mainstream retailers are out and resellers are charging well over list. It's GTA VI demand, and Sony hasn't commented.
points: GAMINGbible, citing Notebookcheck and What Hi-Fi?, reports PS5 stock shortages in the US, UK, parts of Europe and Asia. Currys and John Lewis were out of stock on 25 Nov, and third-party sellers list the PS5 Pro at up to £1,475. This is retail reporting, not a Sony statement.
NielsenIQ: UK PS5 sales rose 46% week-on-week in GTA VI's launch week (19 Nov).
No Sony statement on supply.
stories.next: Black Friday trading today (27 Nov) and the weekend; the next UK weekly chart data (date not announced).

stories.headline: Nature: rumoured AI-lab algorithms said to break public-key encryption, unconfirmed
stories.why: If real it would be among the most consequential results at the AI and mathematics boundary, undermining RSA-style security. Today it is a rumour: no lab has published details.
points: Nature (26 Nov) reports researchers suggesting leading AI labs have found polynomial-time algorithms against public-key cryptography.
Scott Aaronson wrote he is 'virtually certain' the labs hold 'one or more bombshells' but is much less confident about their nature.
RSA, which relies on factoring products of large primes, is one rumoured target.
Nature could not confirm the rumours; a search found no lab confirmation.
stories.next: Watch for lab papers or statements; none scheduled.
